mainTopic: טרפות: a missing vertebra or rib, a crushed skull, the flesh covering the כרס, and clawing (דרוסה) by predators large and small
overview: This amud discusses several injuries that make an animal a טרפה. It begins by settling a clash between two rulings of שמואל. A rib torn out without its vertebra and a vertebra missing without a rib are two separate causes of טרפה, and the second case is found at the end of the flanks. רב then explains why the vertebra dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל is not listed among בית שמאי's leniencies: it was taught about טומאה, where בית שמאי are the strict side. Next, the גמרא asks how to measure a skull crushed 'in its majority', and that question ends in תיקו. It also asks whether a tear in the flesh covering the כרס is enough; a proof from the משנה is tried and rejected. The rest of the amud is about דרוסה, an animal clawed by a predator. רב sets the minimum at a wolf for animals and a hawk for birds. רב חסדא says a cat or mongoose counts against kids and lambs, and a weasel against birds. A ברייתא challenges him, and the גמרא answers in two versions using בריבי's rule about whether rescuers are present, together with the story of the cat at רב כהנא's house. The amud ends as רב כהנא begins to ask רב a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A second statement of שמואל about a missing vertebra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about how much missing spine counts as a deficiency, plus שמואל's statement that the same applies to a טרפה. This sets up a contradiction with שמואל's earlier ruling about a torn-out rib.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much has to be missing from the spine? בית שמאי say two vertebrae, and בית הלל say one vertebra. And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the same is true for a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the contradiction it began earlier. It quotes a ruling about missing vertebrae, and שמואל's statement that this ruling also applies to a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the daf, שמואל said that a rib torn from its root makes the animal a טרפה. Here he speaks only about a missing vertebra, which sounds like the vertebra is what matters. So the two statements of שמואל seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A deficiency, something missing
The spine
A vertebra / vertebrae (the small bones of the spine)
An animal with a fatal injury or defect, which may not be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the second half of a question that started before this section, so it is set against שמואל's earlier rule about a torn-out rib.

phrases.english: How much is a deficiency in the spine?
phrases.notes: This is about a dead body: with this much missing, it no longer counts as a full body for spreading טומאה in a tent.

phrases.english: בית שמאי say: two vertebrae,
and בית הלל say: one vertebra.
And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
And so too for a טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a contradiction against שמואל's earlier ruling about a rib torn from its root.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's earlier ruling that a rib torn from its root makes the animal a טרפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here שמואל speaks of a missing vertebra as the cause of טרפה, which seems to clash with his ruling that a torn-out rib alone is enough.

steps.title: Two different injuries: rib alone or vertebra alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל's two rulings speak about two different cases: a rib torn out without its vertebra, and a vertebra missing without a rib.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is a rib without a vertebra; there it is a vertebra without a rib.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each statement of שמואל is about a different injury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The torn-out rib ruling covers a rib pulled out while the vertebra stays. The missing vertebra ruling covers a vertebra missing where no rib is involved. Each injury makes the animal a טרפה on its own, so the two rulings do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A rib
Here ... there: used to split two sources into two different cases

phrases.english: Here, it is a rib without a vertebra,
phrases.notes: "Here" means שמואל's earlier ruling about the rib torn from its root.

phrases.english: there, it is a vertebra without a rib.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא צֵלָע בְּלֹא חוּלְיָא הָתָם חוּלְיָא בְּלֹא צֵלָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ruling describes a different injury
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought both rulings were about the same injury, so they seemed to contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: A rib torn out without its vertebra, and a vertebra missing without a rib, are each a separate cause of טרפה.

steps.title: Where is there a vertebra with no rib?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that a rib can be torn out without its vertebra, but asks where a vertebra could be missing without a rib attached to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A rib without a vertebra, fine, that happens. But a vertebra without a rib, where would you ever find that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whether the second case in the answer is even possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ribs are attached to vertebrae, so losing a vertebra would seem to always take a rib with it. If so, the case of a vertebra without a rib would not exist, and the answer would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part is fine
How could you find such a case? (asking if a case can really happen)

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא צֵלָע בְּלֹא חוּלְיָא – מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ,
phrases.english: Granted, a rib without a vertebra, you can find it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חוּלְיָא בְּלֹא צֵלָע – הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ?
phrases.english: but a vertebra without a rib, how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא צֵלָע בְּלֹא חוּלְיָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the second case in step 2's answer is realistic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where in the body is there a vertebra that has no rib attached?

steps.title: At the end of the flanks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that at the ends of the flanks there are vertebrae with no ribs attached.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the end of the flanks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the place in the body where a vertebra can be missing without any rib.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Toward the end of the flanks, the spine still has vertebrae, but the ribs have already stopped. So a vertebra missing there involves no rib, and the answer in step 2 holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The end of
The flanks (the sides of the body near the lower back)

steps.whatToRemember: A torn-out rib and a missing vertebra are two separate causes of טרפה. A vertebra without a rib is found at the end of the flanks.

phrases.english: At the end of the flanks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At the end of the flanks there are vertebrae with no ribs attached.

steps.title: Why isn't this among the leniencies of בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא challenges שמואל: if they argue the same way about a טרפה, then בית הלל are the strict side, so the case should appear in the list of 'leniencies of בית שמאי and stringencies of בית הלל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא challenged this: then let the case be taught together with the leniencies of בית שמאי and the stringencies of בית הלל!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא attacks שמואל's statement 'and so too for a טרפה' by pointing to a known list of disputes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a טרפה, finding more things wrong is the strict side. בית הלל say one missing vertebra is enough, so they are stricter than בית שמאי, who need two. Since there is a list of cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict, this case should be in it, but it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it, attacking a statement with a strong objection

keyTerms.term: קוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
keyTerms.meaning: The list of cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict, which goes against their usual pattern

steps.confusionAlert: Usually בית שמאי are the strict ones. That is why a special list exists for the unusual cases where בית הלל are stricter.

phrases.english: רב אושעיא challenged it:
But let him teach it together with the leniencies of בית שמאי
and the stringencies of בית הלל?
phrases.notes: This list of unusual cases is found in מסכת עדיות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to שמואל's statement in step 1 and attacks it from a new angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that the vertebra dispute applies 'so too for a טרפה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it applies to טרפה, then בית הלל are the stricter side, so the case belongs in the list of בית שמאי's leniencies, and it is missing from there.

steps.title: The dispute was first stated about טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the dispute was originally asked and stated about טומאה of a dead body. There בית שמאי are the strict side, so it does not belong in the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: when the question was asked, it was asked about טומאה, where בית שמאי are the strict ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains why the case is missing from the list: the dispute as it was taught is about טומאה, not about טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For טומאה, a body missing less still counts as a full body. בית שמאי need two missing vertebrae before the body stops making things טמא, so they are stricter. The טרפה side is just שמואל's comparison and was never taught directly, so the list ignores it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked
Ritual impurity, here of a dead body
On the strict side

steps.whatToRemember: The vertebra dispute was taught about טומאה, where בית שמאי are stricter. שמואל only compared it to טרפה, so it is not listed among בית שמאי's leniencies.

phrases.english: רב said to him:
When it was asked, it was asked about טומאה,
where בית שמאי are the strict side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אושעיא's challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the original setting of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the dispute should be classified by its טרפה side, where בית הלל are stricter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is classified by its original setting, טומאה, where בית שמאי are stricter, so it does not belong in the list.

steps.title: Returning to שמואל: a skull crushed in its majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another item from שמואל's list: a skull crushed in its majority makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a skull that was crushed in its majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to שמואל's list of טרפות and quotes the next item, a skull crushed in its majority. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new item from שמואל's list, not a continuation of the rib and vertebra discussion. The word 'majority' is unclear, and that is what the next step asks about.

keyTerms.meaning: Skull
Was crushed or pressed in
In its majority, meaning most of it

phrases.english: And a skull that was crushed in its majority.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from שמואל's list of things that make an animal a טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the rib and vertebra discussion and returns to quote another item from שמואל's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal whose skull is crushed in its majority is a טרפה.

steps.title: Majority of height or of circumference? Left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether 'majority' means most of the skull's height or most of its circumference. The question stays open: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: does it mean most of its height, or most of its circumference? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks how to measure 'most' of the skull, by height or by the distance around it. The גמרא has no answer and leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A skull can be measured in two directions, and a crush could cover most of one direction but not the other. Since no source settles it, the גמרא ends with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question it does not yet know the answer to
Most of its height
Most of its circumference, the distance around it
Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו is not an answer. It means the גמרא admits it could not settle the question.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
The majority of its height, or the majority of its circumference?
Let it stand.
phrases.notes: The question stays open. No answer is given.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to measure the 'majority' mentioned in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'majority' of the skull is measured by height or by circumference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer. The question is left as תיקו.

steps.title: שמואל: the flesh covering the כרס damaged in its majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another item from שמואל's list: the flesh covering most of the כרס, if damaged in its majority, makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the flesh that covers most of the כרס, if damaged in its majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in שמואל's list, about the flesh that covers the כרס. This line sets up רב אשי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again the word 'majority' is not defined. Here the open point is what kind of damage counts, a tear or a removal.

keyTerms.meaning: The rumen, the first stomach of an animal that chews its cud
The flesh that covers or wraps around

phrases.english: And the flesh that covers most of the rumen, in its majority.
phrases.notes: It means that most of this covering flesh was damaged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the skull to the next item in שמואל's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If most of the flesh that covers the כרס is damaged, the animal is a טרפה.

steps.title: Is a long tear enough, or must most of the flesh be removed?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether שמואל means a tear along most of the flesh, or only a case where most of the flesh was taken away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: does it mean most of it was torn, or most of it was removed?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks what kind of damage שמואל means. Is a long tear enough, or must most of the flesh actually be gone?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tear leaves all the flesh in place with a long cut through it. Removal means the flesh is actually missing. If only removal counts, a torn animal would stay kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Torn, cut along its length while the flesh is still there
Removed, taken away entirely

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
With most of it torn, or with most of it removed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what kind of damage counts in the case from step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a tear along most of the covering flesh is enough to make the animal a טרפה, or only removal of most of it.

steps.title: A proof from the משנה about the outer כרס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer from a משנה that says a tear in most of the 'outer כרס' makes the animal a טרפה. In ארץ ישראל, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explained that the 'outer כרס' is the flesh covering the כרס. So a tear in that flesh is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Resolve it from what we learned in a משנה: if the inner כרס was pierced, or most of the outer one was torn, the animal is a טרפה. And in the West they said in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: the whole כרס is the inner כרס. So which is the outer כרס? The flesh that covers most of the כרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רב אשי's question from a משנה, together with how רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explained it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the word 'torn' for the outer כרס. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the outer כרס is the covering flesh. Put together, a tear in most of the covering flesh, not only its removal, makes the animal a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolve, settle the open question
The inner כרס
The outer כרס
In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Resolve it from what we learned in a mishna:
An inner rumen that was perforated,
or where most of the outer one was torn,
and they said in the West
in the name of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַכָּרֵס כּוּלּוֹ זוֹ הִיא כָּרֵס הַפְּנִימִי,
phrases.english: The entire rumen, all of it, is the inner rumen,
and which is the outer rumen?
The flesh that covers most of the rumen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רב אשי's question from step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That a tear in most of the flesh covering the כרס is enough to make the animal a טרפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a tear in most of the outer כרס, as explained by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Rejected: שמואל explains the inner כרס differently
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. שמואל himself, as reported by רבי יעקב בר נחמני, defines the inner כרס as the part with no 'wool'. So for שמואל, the משנה's outer כרס is part of the כרס itself, not the covering flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question is only according to שמואל's view, and this is what רבי יעקב בר נחמני said in the name of שמואל: the inner כרס is the place that has no 'wool'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's explanation of the משנה is not how שמואל explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the inner and outer כרס are two parts of the כרס itself: one without 'wool' and one with it. So the משנה's word 'torn' is about the כרס, not the covering flesh, and it tells us nothing about שמואל's covering-flesh case. רב אשי's question is left without proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Is the reason anything other than...? Used to push away a proof by showing it does not apply to the opinion in question
Wool, here the soft, fuzzy lining inside part of the כרס

steps.whatToRemember: You cannot prove שמואל's rule about the covering flesh from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's explanation of the משנה, because שמואל defines inner and outer כרס differently.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think שמואל's 'outer כרס' is the covering flesh. For שמואל, both inner and outer are parts of the כרס itself.

phrases.english: Is the reason for the question anything other than
phrases.notes: רב אשי's question (is most of it torn, or most of it missing?) only comes up according to שמואל, who explains the inner כרס differently.

phrases.english: according to Shmuel?

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: this is what Rabbi Yaakov bar Nachmani said that Shmuel said:
The place that has no wool.
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's definition of the inner כרס. The 'wool' is the fuzzy lining on part of the כרס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה, as far as שמואל's rule is concerned.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof relies on רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's definition of the outer כרס. שמואל uses a different definition, so the משנה says nothing about his covering-flesh case.

steps.title: רב's size rule for predators that claw
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'clawed by a wolf'. רב sets a minimum: for animals, a wolf or bigger, and for birds, a hawk or bigger.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'and an animal clawed by a wolf.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: for animals, it counts from a wolf and up. For birds, it counts from a hawk and up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case from the משנה, an animal clawed by a predator. It brings רב's rule about how strong the predator must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב sets a lower limit. A predator as strong as a wolf or stronger can make an animal a טרפה by clawing it. For birds, the lower limit is a hawk. This rule sets up the next question: what weaker predator is רב trying to leave out?

keyTerms.meaning: Clawing: when a predator attacks an animal with its claws
A hawk
And upward, meaning that animal and anything stronger

phrases.english: "And [an animal] clawed by a wolf."
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
With an animal: from a wolf and upward,
and with birds: from a hawk and upward.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְרוּסַת הַזְּאֵב. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, דרוסה, after the discussion of the flesh covering the כרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For animals, clawing by a wolf or any stronger predator makes the animal a טרפה. For birds, clawing by a hawk or any stronger predator makes the bird a טרפה.

steps.title: What does רב's rule leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'from a wolf and up' excludes. If it excludes a cat, the משנה already taught that by naming the wolf.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רב trying to exclude? If you say a cat, we already learned that in the משנה: 'clawed by a wolf'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's rule. It looks like רב is not telling us anything new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'from a wolf and up' is meant to rule out a weaker animal, like a cat. But the משנה already named the wolf, which already implies a weaker animal does not count. So the גמרא wants to know what new point רב is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude what? Meaning, what case does this rule leave out?
If you say, used to suggest a possible answer that will then be rejected
A cat

phrases.english: To exclude what?
If you say, to exclude a cat,
we already learned: "and clawed by a wolf"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's statement from step 13 as saying nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule 'from the wolf and up' (step 13)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leaving out a cat is already clear from the משנה's words 'clawed by a wolf', so רב's statement would add nothing.

steps.title: Maybe רב teaches that a wolf counts even for large animals
steps.stepSummary: A possible answer: רב is teaching that a wolf's clawing makes even a large animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say this is what רב teaches us: that a wolf's clawing counts even for a large animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible new point in רב's rule. This answer is about to be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that רב's real point is about the victim. Wolf-clawing works not only on small animals like sheep but also on large ones like cattle. That would be something the משנה did not say clearly.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say, which brings up a possible answer
He teaches us, meaning this is the new point
A large domestic animal, such as cattle

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
phrases.english: And if you say, this is what he teaches us:
that a wolf also claws [effectively] a large animal,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives רב's statement a new point: it is about the size of the victim.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's rule would add nothing, because the משנה already leaves out a cat.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב teaches that a wolf's clawing makes even a large animal a טרפה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says a wolf counts only for small animals
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is pushed away from the משנה, where רבי יהודה says a wolf counts for small animals and a lion for large ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: רבי יהודה says, clawing by a wolf counts for a small animal, and clawing by a lion counts for a large animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from step 15 by quoting רבי יהודה in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says a large animal becomes a טרפה only from a lion's clawing. So a wolf is not strong enough for a large animal. That goes against the idea that רב teaches a wolf works even on a large animal.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, which brings up a contradicting source
A small domestic animal, such as a sheep or goat
A lion

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
clawing by a wolf, with a small animal,
and clawing by a lion, with a large animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that a wolf's clawing makes a large animal a טרפה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה in the משנה says only a lion's clawing counts for a large animal.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יהודה disagrees with the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: A possible way out: רבי יהודה is arguing with the חכמים, and רב follows the חכמים, who hold that a wolf counts even for large animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that רבי יהודה disagrees with the חכמים...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to save the answer from step 15. This suggestion is about to be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה's view is his own opinion against the חכמים, then the חכמים might hold that a wolf works even on large animals. רב could be following the חכמים, so step 15's answer would still work.

keyTerms.meaning: He really disagrees, meaning he holds a separate opinion

phrases.english: And if you say
that Rabbi Yehuda disagrees,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִפְלָג פְּלִיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 16 by treating רבי יהודה as a separate opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the opposing source to one opinion that רב does not follow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's words show that everyone holds a wolf does not count for large animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה's view is his own. The חכמים, and רב with them, hold that a wolf counts even for large animals.

steps.title: רבי אלעא: רבי יהודה only explains the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: This is pushed away. רבי אלעא says רבי יהודה does not disagree. He is only explaining what the חכמים meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי בנימין בר יפת said in the name of רבי אלעא: רבי יהודה came only to explain the words of the חכמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that רבי יהודה disagrees with the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה is only explaining the חכמים, then the חכמים agree that a wolf counts only for small animals. So no one is left who says a wolf works on a large animal, and the challenge against step 15 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: To explain

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet say that Rabbi Ela said:
Rabbi Yehuda did not come
except to explain the words of the Sages!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion from step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי יהודה argues with the חכמים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אלעא says רבי יהודה only explains the חכמים, so everyone agrees a wolf counts only for small animals.

steps.title: One אמורא cannot disprove another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעא's view does not bind רב. רב can hold that רבי יהודה really disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you throwing the words of one man against another man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 15's answer. רבי אלעא is just one opinion, and רב may simply see it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעא's claim that רבי יהודה only explains the חכמים is his own reading. רב is allowed to disagree and read רבי יהודה as a separate opinion. So רב can follow the חכמים and say a wolf counts even for large animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Are you setting one man against another? An opinion of one אמורא cannot disprove a different אמורא

phrases.english: Are you setting one man against another man?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 18 and brings back the answers of steps 15 and 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement between אמוראים: one אמורא's view does not disprove another.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעא's statement proves that רב cannot hold a wolf counts for large animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב may disagree with רבי אלעא and hold that רבי יהודה argues with the חכמים.

steps.title: Second answer: רב really is excluding a cat
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רב does come to exclude a cat. Without רב, we might think the משנה named the wolf only because it is the usual attacker.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say instead: really, רב comes to exclude a cat. You might have thought the משנה mentions the wolf only because that is how it usually happens. So רב teaches us that a cat does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the first question in step 14. It goes back to the cat after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's word 'wolf' might only describe the common case, not set a strict minimum. Then a cat might count too, at least for a small animal. רב's words 'from the wolf and up' make it clear that the wolf really is the lower limit, so a cat is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say, which brings a second, different answer
Really, which goes back to an idea that was first set aside
You might have said, describing the mistaken thought being corrected
The usual way of things, meaning the common case and not a strict rule

steps.whatToRemember: For דרוסה, רב sets a lower limit: a wolf for animals and a hawk for birds. Either רב teaches that a wolf counts even for large animals, following the view that רבי יהודה argues with the חכמים, or רב teaches that a cat does not count, since the משנה's 'wolf' is a real limit and not just the usual case.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the second answer means a wolf counts for large animals. In this answer everyone agrees a wolf counts only for small animals, and רב's point is only to exclude the cat.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
Actually, it is to exclude a cat,
because you might have said
that it teaches the usual way of things,
so he teaches us [that it is not so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question in step 14, different from the line of steps 15 to 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rules out a mistaken reading: the משנה's case is a real limit, not just the usual case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה mentions the wolf only as the common attacker, so a cat might also make a small animal a טרפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב teaches that the wolf is the real minimum, so a cat's clawing does not make an animal a טרפה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: cat and mongoose for kids and lambs, weasel for birds
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a cat or mongoose's claw attack counts for kids and lambs, and a weasel's claw attack counts for birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said in the name of רב חסדא: a claw attack by a cat or a mongoose counts on kids and lambs. A claw attack by a weasel counts on birds.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens. רב חסדא lists smaller predators and the victims their claw attack can make טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא dealt with the wolf and the lion. רב חסדא adds smaller hunters. Each one counts only against animals small enough for it: a cat or mongoose against young sheep and goats, and a weasel against birds.

keyTerms.meaning: A claw attack by a predator, which can make the victim טרפה
Cat
Mongoose
Weasel
Young goats and lambs

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Amram said that Rav Chisda said:
The claw attack of a cat and a mongoose
counts on kids and lambs;
phrases.notes: "Counts" means the victim becomes a טרפה.

phrases.english: the claw attack of a weasel counts on birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the wolf and lion discussion, a new statement about smaller predators
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cat and mongoose: their claw attack counts on kids and lambs. Weasel: its claw attack counts on birds.

steps.title: A teaching says a cat's claw attack does not count
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a cat, hawk, or mongoose makes an animal טרפה only if it actually pierces through. That suggests their claw attack alone does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'The claw attack of a cat, hawk, or mongoose does not count until the wound is pierced through to the hollow.' This implies they have no power of claw attack!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from a ברייתא. That source treats a cat's attack like any ordinary wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real דרוסה makes the animal טרפה even without a hole. The ברייתא requires a full puncture for these animals, so their claw attack has no special power. That clashes with רב חסדא, who said a cat's claw attack does count.

keyTerms.meaning: Hawk
Until it is pierced through into the body's hollow
They do not have

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The claw attack of a cat, a hawk, and a mongoose
does not count until it is pierced through to the hollow,
but a claw attack, they do not have!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that a cat's claw attack counts for kids and lambs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires a full puncture for a cat, which implies a cat has no power of דרוסה

steps.title: But a hawk's claw attack does count in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ברייתא itself. Our משנה says a hawk's claw attack does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do you really think a hawk does not claw? But we learned in the משנה: 'and the claw attack of a hawk'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses on a side problem. The ברייתא says a hawk has no claw attack, but the משנה says it does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed the hawk together with the cat and mongoose as animals with no real claw attack. Our משנה lists the hawk's claw attack as one that counts. So the ברייתא seems to contradict the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so? (introduces a challenge to an assumption)
Claws, attacks with claws

phrases.english: And do you really think a hawk does not claw?
But we learned in the Mishnah: "and the claw attack of the hawk"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side challenge to the ברייתא quoted in the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that a hawk has no claw attack
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה says a hawk's claw attack does count

steps.title: Hawk: counts for birds, not for kids and lambs
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means a hawk attacking birds. The ברייתא means a hawk attacking kids and lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult. Here it is talking about birds; there it is talking about kids and lambs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the hawk contradiction by assigning each source to a different victim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hawk's claw attack is strong enough to count against birds, as the משנה says. It is not strong enough against larger kids and lambs, as the ברייתא says. So the ברייתא is speaking about kids and lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not a difficulty
Here... there (splitting between two cases)
Birds

phrases.english: That is not difficult:
here, regarding birds;
there, regarding kids and lambs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hawk contradiction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה seem to disagree about whether a hawk can claw
steps.terutzMaskana: A hawk's claw attack counts for birds but not for kids and lambs

steps.title: רב חסדא is still challenged
steps.stepSummary: Even with the hawk answer, the ברייתא now speaks about kids and lambs. It says a cat does not count for them, which still contradicts רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult for רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main challenge from Step 22. It points out that the hawk answer actually makes the problem sharper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the ברייתא is about kids and lambs. In that same case it says a cat has no claw attack. But רב חסדא said a cat's claw attack does count for kids and lambs, so the clash is now direct.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, regardless

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult for Rav Chisda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the challenge of Step 22, made stronger by Step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling about cats and kids or lambs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, now understood as speaking about kids and lambs, says a cat has no claw attack against them

steps.title: רב חסדא follows בריבי: it counts when people try to rescue
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא follows a תנא called בריבי. In his view, a cat's claw attack counts only where people are trying to rescue the victim.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to this תנא, as it was taught: בריבי says: They only said there is no claw attack in a place where people are not rescuing. But where people are rescuing, there is a claw attack.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא relies on a different ברייתא. That source limits the 'no claw attack' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בריבי, the ברייתא's rule that a cat has no claw attack applies only when nobody tries to save the victim. When people are rescuing, the cat's attack does count. רב חסדא's ruling is speaking about that second situation.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with this תנא
People trying to rescue the victim

phrases.english: He said it according to this Tanna,
as it was taught: Berabi says:
They only said there is no claw attack
in a place where there are none rescuing,
but in a place where there are people rescuing,
there is a claw attack.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רב חסדא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relying on a different תנא who limits the rule to one situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A cat never has a claw attack against kids and lambs
steps.terutzMaskana: A cat's claw attack counts when people are trying to rescue the victim, and רב חסדא is speaking about that case
steps.confusionAlert: בריבי does not argue that a cat always has a claw attack. He agrees there is none when nobody is rescuing, and he says it counts only when people are rescuing.

steps.title: The story of the cat at רב כהנא's house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions בריבי's limit. A cat at רב כהנא's house, with nobody rescuing, still left blood on a door after striking it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where nobody is rescuing, there is no claw attack? But there was a hen in רב כהנא's house that a cat chased. It went into a small room and the door shut in the cat's face. The cat struck the door with its paws, and five drops of blood were found on the door!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בריבי's idea that a cat's attack counts only when people are rescuing. It brings a real-life story as evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this story nobody was trying to save the hen. Even so, the cat was frustrated and left drops of blood on the door when it struck it with its paws. That suggests a cat's claws are harmful even with no rescuers present, which seems to undo בריבי's limit.

keyTerms.meaning: That ran (chased)
A small inner room
Its paws
Drops of blood

phrases.english: And in a place where there are none rescuing, there is no claw attack?
But there was that hen
phrases.notes: Some versions have the Hebrew word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the Aramaic word in square brackets. Both mean "hen."

phrases.english: that was in Rav Kahana's house,
that a cat ran after it,
and it went into a small room,
and the door shut in its face,
phrases.notes: The door closed on the cat, so it never got to the hen.

phrases.english: and it struck the door with its paws,
and five drops of blood were found on it!
phrases.notes: "On it" means on the door. The point is that the cat's claws carried something harmful even with nobody rescuing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit introduced by בריבי in the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: בריבי's rule that a cat has no claw attack when nobody is rescuing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the story nobody was rescuing, yet the angry cat's paws left blood on the door, so its claws are harmful even then

steps.title: A cat defending itself counts like rescuers being present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from רב כהנא's cat. When a cat is protecting itself, it counts as if people were trying to rescue the victim.
steps.simpleTranslation: Saving itself is also considered like others trying to save the victim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends בריבי against the story of the cat at רב כהנא's house. The door was shut in the cat's face, so it felt threatened and was fighting for itself, and that counts like a rescue situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בריבי said a cat's claw attack only counts when people are trying to rescue the victim, because then the cat attacks hard. A cat that has a door shut in its face is also under pressure, so it attacks just as hard. The blood on the door therefore fits בריבי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: saving itself; the cat is protecting itself
others trying to save the victim from the cat
is like, is considered the same as

phrases.english: Saving itself also
phrases.notes: Here "itself" means the cat. The door slammed in its face, so it felt it had to defend itself.

phrases.english: is considered like others trying to save [the victim],

steps.triggerLanguage: הַצָּלַת עַצְמָהּ נָמֵי כְּהַצָּלַת אֲחֵרִים דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 27 from רב כהנא's cat.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening the definition: a cat defending itself counts as a rescue situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nobody was rescuing the hen, so under בריבי the cat's attack should not have been strong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Self-defense also makes the cat attack hard, so it fits into בריבי's category of 'where there are rescuers'.

steps.title: How the רבנן explain the blood on the door
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן of the ברייתא explain the blood. They answer that a cat does have venom, but its venom is not strong enough to make the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? A cat has venom, but its venom does not burn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן, who say a cat's attack never counts for kids and lambs. They are asked about the blood, and they answer that the venom is real but too weak to matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'five drops of blood' showed that a cat has venom. The רבנן agree that it has venom. They hold that this venom does not burn strongly enough to ruin a kid or a lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: venom, the poison in an attacking animal's claws
does not burn

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן do not deny that a cat has venom. They only say the venom is too weak to make the animal a טרפה.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
It has venom,
but its venom does not burn.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן זִיהֲרָא אִית לֵיהּ וְלָא קָלֵי זִיהֲרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from בריבי's answer to the other opinion and explains the same story according to the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the facts: having venom is different from having venom strong enough to matter.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The blood seems to prove that a cat's attack is dangerous enough to count.
steps.terutzMaskana: A cat has venom, but it is too weak to make a kid or a lamb a טרפה.
steps.whatToRemember: First version: בריבי says a cat counts only when it is pressured, and self-defense counts as pressure. The רבנן say a cat's venom is too weak to count at all.

steps.title: A second version: the ברייתא itself follows בריבי
steps.stepSummary: Some tell the discussion differently. The ברייתא that says a cat does not count for kids and lambs is בריבי's view, and it is talking about a case with no rescuers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is בריבי's, as it was taught: בריבי says, they only said a claw attack counts where there are rescuers, but where there are no rescuers, it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of how it answered the contradiction with רב חסדא. In this version, the ברייתא that challenged רב חסדא is said to follow בריבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב חסדא himself followed בריבי. In this version, the ברייתא is בריבי's, and it only means a case where nobody is rescuing. רב חסדא follows the other view, that a cat's claw attack counts on kids and lambs even with no rescuers, so the ברייתא no longer forces a contradiction with him.

keyTerms.meaning: whose opinion is this?
a claw attack by a predator that can make the animal a טרפה
people trying to rescue the victim

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions use בריבי, but in different ways. In the first, רב חסדא follows בריבי. In the second, the ברייתא is בריבי's, so it does not argue with רב חסדא.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Whose [view] is this? It is בריבי's,
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא saying a cat does not count for kids and lambs, which was used against רב חסדא.

phrases.english: as it was taught: בריבי says:
They only said there is a claw attack
in a place where there are rescuers,
but in a place where there are no rescuers,
there is no claw attack.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי הָא מַנִּי בְּרִיבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the answer in Step 26 by moving בריבי from רב חסדא to the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ברייתא to one תנא and limiting it to a specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says in general that a cat never counts for kids and lambs, which goes against רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is בריבי's and only speaks about a case where nobody is rescuing, so רב חסדא can still hold his view.

steps.title: The cat at רב כהנא's house challenges בריבי again
steps.stepSummary: Inside the second version, the גמרא brings the same challenge. A cat with nobody rescuing still left blood on a door.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where there are no rescuers, is there really no claw attack? But there was a hen at רב כהנא's house. A cat chased it and went into a small room, the door shut in its face, it struck the door with its paw, and five drops of blood were found on the door.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the story of רב כהנא's cat, this time as a challenge inside the second version. The point is that a cat with no rescuers around still struck with venom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בריבי said that with no rescuers, a cat's attack does not count. In the story, nobody was rescuing the hen, yet the cat's paw left blood, which shows it has real venom. This seems to prove that a cat's attack can matter even with no rescuers.

keyTerms.meaning: door

phrases.english: And in a place where there are no rescuers, there is no claw attack?
But there was that hen
phrases.notes: Some versions have the Hebrew word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the Aramaic word in square brackets. Both mean "hen."

phrases.english: that was in the house of רב כהנא,
which a cat ran after,
and it went into a small room,
and the door shut in its face,
and it struck the door with its paw,
and five drops of blood were found on it.
phrases.notes: "On it" means on the door. The blood shows the cat's paw carries venom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין מַצִּילִין אֵין דְּרוּסָה וְהָא הָהִיא תַּרְנְגוֹלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges בריבי's rule as it was quoted in the second version (Step 30). The גמרא repeats the challenge from Step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: בריבי's rule that with no rescuers, a cat's attack does not count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real story with no rescuers shows the cat still struck with venom, which goes against בריבי's limit.

steps.title: Same answer again: self-defense counts like rescuers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer in the second version. A cat protecting itself counts as if rescuers were present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Saving itself is also considered like others trying to save the victim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in the second version with the same idea as before. The cat that had the door shut in its face was defending itself, so this was not really a 'no rescuers' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בריבי's 'no rescuers' case means a calm cat that is under no pressure. A cat with a door slammed in its face is under pressure, just as when people chase it. So the story does not disprove בריבי.

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the story of רב כהנא's cat is answered the same way: a cat defending itself counts like a cat facing rescuers.

phrases.english: Saving itself also
is considered like others trying to save [the victim].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 31, using the same answer as Step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening the definition of a rescue situation to include self-defense.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nobody was rescuing the hen, so the case looks like 'no rescuers'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Self-defense counts as rescuers being present, so בריבי's rule stands.

steps.title: רב כהנא asks רב a question

steps.deeperAnalysis: The cat discussion is finished, and a new question is about to begin. רב כהנא now asks his teacher רב about another case.
